title: Contributing Guidelines
text: Please write great commit message. Separate subject body blank line Limit subject line 50 characters Capitalize subject line end subject line period Use imperative mood subject line (example: “Fix networking issue”) Wrap body 72 characters Use body explain , (code shows !) applicable, prefix title relevant component name. (examples: “[Docs] Fix typo”, “[Profile] Fix missing avatar”)
code: [TAG] Short summary of changes in 50 chars or less  Add a more detailed explanation here, if necessary. Possibly give some background about the issue being fixed, etc. The body of the commit message can be several paragraphs. Further paragraphs come after blank lines and please do proper word-wrap.  Wrap it to about 72 characters or so. In some contexts, the first line is treated as the subject of the commit and the rest of the text as the body. The blank line separating the summary from the body is critical (unless you omit the body entirely); various tools like `log`, `shortlog` and `rebase` can get confused if you run the two together.  Explain the problem that this commit is solving. Focus on why you are making this change as opposed to how or what. The code explains how or what. Reviewers and your future self can read the patch, but might not understand why a particular solution was implemented. Are there side effects or other unintuitive consequences of this change? Here's the place to explain them.   - Bullet points are okay, too   - A hyphen or asterisk should be used for the bullet, preceded    by a single space, with blank lines in between  Note the fixed or relevant GitHub issues at the end:  Resolves: #123 See also: #456, #789

title: FLAMES 2.3.1
text: Individual steps can submitted HPC jobs via crew crew.cluster packages, simply supply list crew controllers (named step name) controllers argument pipeline constructors. example, run alignment steps controllers, keeping rest main R session. run_FLAMES() submit alignment step crew controller. default, run_step() ignore crew controllers run step main R session, since easier debug. can use run_step(pipeline, step_name, disable_controller = FALSE) prevent behavior run step crew controllers available. can tailor resources step specifying different arguments controllers. alignment step typically benifits cores (e.g. 64 cores 20GB memory), whereas steps might need much cores memory hungry. See also crew.cluster website information supported job schedulers.
code: # example_pipeline provides an example pipeline for each of the three types # of pipelines: BulkPipeline, SingleCellPipeline and MultiSampleSCPipeline mspipeline <- example_pipeline("MultiSampleSCPipeline") #> Writing configuration parameters to:  /tmp/Rtmp3cGsyz/file440e2d297f5d/config_file_17422.json #> Configured steps:  #>  barcode_demultiplex: TRUE #>  genome_alignment: TRUE #>  gene_quantification: TRUE #>  isoform_identification: TRUE #>  read_realignment: TRUE #>  transcript_quantification: TRUE #> samtools not found, will use Rsamtools package instead # Providing a single controller will run all steps in it: controllers(mspipeline) <- crew::crew_controller_local() # Setting controllers to an empty list will run all steps in the main R session: controllers(mspipeline) <- list() # Alternatively, we can run only the alignment steps in the crew controller: controllers(mspipeline)[["genome_alignment"]] <- crew::crew_controller_local(workers = 4) # Or `controllers(mspipeline) <- list(genome_alignment = crew::crew_cluster())` # to remove controllers for all other steps. # Replace `crew_controller_local()` with `crew.cluster::crew_controller_slurm()` or other # crew controllers according to your HPC job scheduler. # An example helper function to create a Slurm controller with specific resources create_slurm_controller <- function(     cpus, memory_gb, workers = 10, seconds_idle = 10,     script_lines = "module load R/flexiblas/4.5.0") {   name <- sprintf("slurm_%dc%dg", cpus, memory_gb)   crew.cluster::crew_controller_slurm(     name = name,     workers = workers,     seconds_idle = seconds_idle,     retry_tasks = FALSE,     options_cluster = crew.cluster::crew_options_slurm(       script_lines = script_lines,       memory_gigabytes_required = memory_gb,       cpus_per_task = cpus,       log_output = file.path("logs", "crew_log_%A.txt"),       log_error = file.path("logs", "crew_log_%A.txt")     )   ) } controllers(mspipeline)[["genome_alignment"]] <-   create_slurm_controller(cpus = 64, memory_gb = 20)

title: Pipeline for Single Cell Data — SingleCellPipeline
text: FLAMES.SingleCellPipeline object. pipeline can run using run_FLAMES(pipeline). results can accessed experiment(pipeline). pipeline also outputs number output files given outdir directory. output files include: matched_reads.fastq - fastq file reads demultiplexed align2genome.bam - sorted BAM file reads aligned genome matched_reads_dedup.fastq - demultiplexed UMI-deduplicated fastq file transcript_assembly.fa - transcript sequence isoforms isoform_annotated.filtered.gff3 - isoforms gff3 format (also contained SingleCellExperiment) realign2transcript.bam - sorted realigned BAM file using transcript_assembly.fa reference

title: Pipeline for Single Cell Data — SingleCellPipeline
text: default pipeline starts demultiplexing input fastq data. cell barcodes known apriori (e.g. via coupled short-read sequencing), barcodes_file argument can used specify file containing cell barcodes, modified Rcpp version flexiplex used; otherwise, expect_cell_number need provided, BLAZE used generate cell barcodes. pipeline aligns reads genome using minimap2. alignment used isoform detection (either using FLAMES bambu, can configured). reads realigned detected isoforms. Finally, transcript count matrix generated (either using FLAMES's simplistic counting oarfish's Expectation Maximization algorithm, can configured). results can accssed experiment(pipeline). pipeline errored / new steps configured, can resumed calling resume_FLAMES(pipeline)

title: FLAMES Differential Transcript Usage Analysis — sc_DTU_analysis
text: sce SingleCellExperiment object, transcript counts counts slot cluster labels colLabels slot. gene_col column name rowData slot sce contains gene ID / name. Default "gene_id". min_count minimum total counts transcript tested. threads Number threads use parallel processing. method method use testing, listed details. permuations Number permutations permutation methods.

title: FLAMES Differential Transcript Usage Analysis — sc_DTU_analysis
text: tibble containing following columns: p.value - raw p-value adj.p.value - multiple testing adjusted p-value cluster - cluster DTU observed transcript - rowname sce, DTU isoform transcript_usage - transcript usage isoform cluster Additional columns method = "trascript usage permutation": transcript_usage_elsewhere - transcript usage clusters usage_difference - difference two transcript usage permuted_var - variance usage difference permuted data Additional columns method = "chisq": X_value - test statistic df - degrees freedom expected_usage - expected usage (mean across clusters) usage_difference - difference observed expected usage table sorted P-values.

title: FLAMES Differential Transcript Usage Analysis — sc_DTU_analysis
text: Genes 2 isoforms expressing min_count counts selected testing one following methods: trascript usage permutation Transcript usage taken test statistic, cluster labels permuted generate null distribution. chisq Chi-square test transcript count matrix gene. Adjusted P-values calculated Benjamini–Hochberg correction.
